state.description: A low in the Gulf of Alaska will will bring a front to the Alaska Range and Central Interior Tuesday and Wednesday. There is uncertainty with the exact strength and placement of this front and we are currently expecting around 3 to 6 inches of snow from the Western Alaska Range to Fairbanks. However, there is a 30% chance for snow accumulations exceeding 6 inches in this area. Currently, the greatest likelihood of this occurring is towards Eielson AFB and areas east, where Winter Storm Watches are in effect. If the front is a bit farther to the west, this chance increases dramatically in/around Fairbanks. There may end up being a west to east gradient where Eielson gets 6 inches or more of snow, and Fairbanks south/west only gets a couple of inches. We will be monitoring this storm very closely and will have more information as the details become clearer.

state.description: ...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 PM THIS EVENING TO 11 AM PDT FRIDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTH BAY INTERIOR MOUNTAINS... .Moderate offshore winds will develop Thursday evening into Friday morning over the North Bay Interior Mountains. Conditions will be very dry with very poor overnight humidity recoveries only reaching 14 to 24 percent. Rapid fire spread is possible given the combination of gusty northerly winds and very dry overnight conditions. The National Weather Service in San Francisco CA has issued a Red Flag Warning in effect from 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday. * AFFECTED AREA...North Bay Interior Mountains. * TIMING...From 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday. * WINDS 20 FOOT...North winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph. The highest peaks above 4000ft will see gusts up to 60 mph. * RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 16 to 20 percent. * IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
state.instruction: A Red Flag Warning is issued when weather conditions that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening are forecast. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to receive information from authorities. Please advise responding agencies or fire crews in the field of this fire weather alert. Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire. Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks. Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember, one less spark, one less flame. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan! Where will you go? How will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more information.

state.description: ...RED FLAG WATCH FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY... .With the ongoing drought conditions, we have KBDI values well into the 700s, with 10-hour and 100-hour fuel moisture values hovering around 25%. Subsidence behind the front will further dry out the already dry continental air mass, leading to a significant drop in dew points following the front. The forecast drops RH values below 30% across central Louisiana and the interior portions of southeast Texas. Friday through Sunday look to be concerning for fire weather. However, Saturday appears to be the most critical day as the dry, subsided airmass becomes fully entrenched over the highly dried out fuels. This setup is similar to the weather conditions that sparked the Tiger Island fire in 2023, and fires that do spark could quickly spread out of control.. state.description: Tropical Depression 29W is located 555 miles northeast of Chuuk, moving northwest at 13 mph. A turn more to the west is expected to occur over the next 24 hours. state.description: ...A TYPHOON WATCH IS NOW IN EFFECT FOR THE MARIANAS... .NEW INFORMATION... A Typhoon Watch has now been issued for Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Mariana Islands. .AREAS AFFECTED... This local statement provides important information and recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas. .Watches/Warnings... A Typhoon watch is in effect for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan in the Mariana Islands. A Typhoon Watch means that Typhoon conditions, including winds of 74 mph or greater, are possible within the next 48 hours somewhere within the specified areas. All persons in the watch areas should review their preparedness plan and begin to take actions to prepare for conditions as indicated by your local forecast and additional details. .STORM INFORMATION... At 1 PM ChST...the center of Tropical Depression 29W was located near latitude 10.8N...longitude 158.9E. This was about 970 miles east of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 285 degrees, at 13 mph. 29W is expected to make a turn toward the west over the next couple of days. Storm intensity was 35 mph. 29W is expected to begin to intensify Friday. .SITUATION OVERVIEW... A Typhoon Watch has now been issued. A more detailed statement will follow shortly.
state.instruction: . For those under a watch, now is the time to initiate preparations according to your typhoon disaster plan specific to your home or business. For those nearby, review your typhoon disaster plan and become ready to act if a watch or a warning is later issued for your area. It is important to actively listen for forthcoming information from your local National Weather Service office and emergency management agency.

Invest 96W is currently rated as "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center, meaning tropical cyclone development is likely, but beyond 24 hours. It's currently located west of Ujae near 9.3N 164.4E. It continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of Kosrae/east-northest of Pohnpei. Inflow into the developing disturbance will allow for locally heavy rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per hour rain rates probable from time to time. Rainfall totals will likely be 2 to 5 inches tonight through Thursday, with locally higher amounts possible. Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated wind gusts to 30 knots are possible with any heavy shower or thunderstorm that develops. state.description: ...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE SATURDAY... .A strong cold front will quickly move through the area Friday afternoon. The front will be mostly if not completely dry as it moves through the area. Quickly after it moves into the Gulf much drier air will surge in behind it. In addition cooler air will move in along with strong northerly winds. On Saturday sunny skies and winds in the first 1500-3000 ft will be out of the same direction sllowing for efficient mixing. This will help to bring wind gusts of 15 to as high as 30 miles an hour across most locations along and north of I-10. This will also lead to even drier air mixing into the area helping to drop the RH into the mid to lower 30% range with some locations seeing the relative humidity just below 30%. This will combine with current D1 and D2 drought conditions across all of southwest Mississippi and much of southeast LA along and northwest of a line from Thibodaux to Franklinton. This could provide ample fuel for wildfires. state.description: Invest 96W has been upgraded to Tropical Depression 29W, and is currently located northeast of Pohnpei near 9.6N 161.2E. 29W will continue to develop and strengthen just north of the region, and will generally head towards the Marianas. Convergent fresh to strong westerlies south of 29W's center are producing bands of scattered to numerous showers capable of strong gusts and locally heavy rainfall, across Pohnpei and their coastal waters, and Gusty winds across Kosrae and their costal waters. Ensemble model guidance suggests rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible for Pohnpei through late Friday night as 29W strengthens and passes north of the island. Gusts to 30 knots will be possible near heavier showers. Moderate to strong winds with gusts to near-gale for Kosrae through this afternoon as conditions start to ease there. Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions hazardous to small craft, and inter-island travel is discouraged. For more information on TD 29W, see bulletins issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW and by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM.

state.description: ESFAJK A strong storm system is expected to move over the northern Alaska Panhandle beginning Monday night and continuing through Tuesday. Juneau and Gustavus are expected to see periods of moderate to heavy rain for a majority of the day on Tuesday, resulting in significant and rapid rises on small creeks and streams. Rain totals for this event are around 2-4 inches over a 36 hour period, though expected totals will likely change as the event moves closer. At this time, expect to see similar impacts to the previous storm system we saw on Friday, where Salmon River, Jordan Creek, and Montana Creek reached either near or into minor flood stage. state.description: * WHAT...Tropical storm conditions, including winds of 34 to 63 knots, are expected. Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more are possible within the next 48 hours. * WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters. * WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning late tonight, continuing into at least Sunday night, possibly longer if conditions warrant. * IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that could damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically reducing visibilities in heavy rain. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly toward the Marianas. state.instruction: Prepare for tropical storm force conditions Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions are expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely dangerous for any vessels of larger size. As Tropical Storm Champi approaches the Marianas, stay in safe harbor.

state.description: Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall to the area. The first ongoing front is expected to bring 1 to 2 inches of rain to the Juneau area the rest of today, with the second round of heavy rain bringing an additional 1 to 2 inches through tonight. More localized higher amounts are possible due to terrain effects, but overall the moderate to heavy rainfall is expected to last into the overnight hours and Friday morning with not much of a break between the rounds of precipitation. The precipitation amounts that have fallen today and the additional forecasted amounts expected through Friday morning are expected to bring rises to small creeks and rivers in the area. While small creeks and rivers may reach bankfull, there is no flooding anticipated at this time. Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the situation and update our forecast. For Jordan Creek near Juneau: At 11:00am the stage was 7.8 feet. Flood Stage is 9.7 feet. Forecast: A crest around 9.9 feet is expected around 1:00pm Friday. Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around 10:00am Friday. Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around 10:00pm Friday. state.description: Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle. The first ongoing front is expected to bring 1 to 1.5 inches of rain to the northern half of the panhandle today. The second round of heavy rain is expected to bring an additional 0.5 to 1.5 inches tonight into Friday morning, with the higher end QPF amounts expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands. More localized lower or higher amounts are possible due to terrain effects. A brief lull in the heavier precipitation amounts is expected during the afternoon hours today. Even higher rain amounts are possible for parts of the central panhandle associated with the front tonight as its low develops inland and moves northward, though there is still a lack of confidence on the exact location of these higher rates. As of now, the highest amounts are expected to move into southern Baranof Island up into Stephens Passage, though some elevated rainfall amounts may still reach Sitka and other parts of the central and northern panhandle. While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding anticipated at this time. Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the situation and update our forecast.

state.description: The National Weather Service in Jackson has issued a Red Flag Warning, which is in effect from 9 AM to 8 PM CDT Friday. A Fire Weather Watch has also been issued. This Fire Weather Watch is in effect from Saturday morning through Saturday evening. * WIND...North winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph behind a cold front. * HUMIDITY...Minimum Relative Humidity values between 25 to 40 percent. * FUELS...Critically dry. * IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
state.instruction: A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures will create favorable weather for rapid fire growth and spread. Avoid activities that promote open flames and sparks. A Fire Weather Watch means that the potential for critical fire weather conditions exists. These conditions could promote the rapid spread of wildfires which could become life-threatening. Check www.weather.gov/jan/fireweather for forecast updates and a possible upgrade of this watch to a Red Flag Warning.
